title: feat: the improvement list is kept as data, and a release is checked
headline: A project's improvement list and roadmap now live as data: each row has one tag, says who caught it and where its numbers were measured, and the roadmap, counts and rows are generated from it. A release is called done only when a check has read every step on GitHub and in the project.
alignment: v1.35.0 is the second v2.0 step for tracking (T4): after the next action and the decisions in 1.34.0, the list and the roadmap.

items.text: The improvement list lives in _List.jsonl, one row per line with one tag; state.mjs lists the open rows, adds and changes rows, and imports a markdown list once, whole or not at all.
items.after: One row per line, one tag

items.text: The roadmap table with the open rows per step, the tag counts and the rows are generated between list markers; a hand edit is refused and the check fails on it.
items.before: Recounted by hand at each closeout

items.text: Each closed row names who caught it and whether it slipped past a gate, and each number names where it was measured; list caught prints the catch rate and found to shipped by origin.
At the same severity, rows found in real projects rank above rows the owner asked for, then those from other methods, then the kit's own finds.

release-check.mjs reads each release step (PR merged, main CI green on the merge commit, the tag on its files, the notes published, the state check) and names every one missing; the closeout calls nothing done until it passes.
ci-wait.mjs reports each CI run's end in one line, green or red, with one line past ten minutes; the PR body skill starts it after each push.
The build record writes the release notes draft, split into what projects get and what stays in the kit; publishing stays the owner's tap.

verification: Every new test failed on the code before it: 9 list tests on 1.34.0's state script, the release and CI tests and the notes test before their code existed.
On a copy of the workbench list, the import moved 342 rows and 17 roadmap steps, and the generated counts equal the hand recount; it first refused 32 rows the list itself had broken.

decisions.decision: The list as data with no rule text
decisions.why: The owner picked option A by pop-up: the labels live in the data and the check, so no recall run was needed while the machine was busy.

decisions.decision: Imported rows owe their labels to one audit
decisions.why: Failing 222 old rows at once would block every closeout; rows added or closed from now on must carry them, and list audit names the rest.
The owner asked that builds take in aligned work: the release check, the CI report and the notes draft ride with the list.

upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A project with a markdown improvement list moves it once with the state script's `list import`, which names any row it cannot move.
limits: Rows moved from a markdown list keep their numbers and finders unlabelled until list audit is worked through. The release check cannot tell whether the notes say true things.

tests.flips: declared tests on main and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
